newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Monday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by light marketings and firm demand, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants. Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants.

Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $56.50 to $57.00 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants, although prices could turn higher as the day progresses if packers compete more aggressively for hogs, an Indiana dealer said.
The demand for tight hog supplies was seen offsetting potential weakness from expected light slaughter Monday due to floating holidays at several plants, dealers and packer buyers said.

Hormel Food Corp's pork processing plant in Austin, Minn., and hog slaughtering plant in Fremont, Neb, will be closed along with Quality Pork Processing Inc's hog slaughter plant in Austin, which provides pork for Hormel's Austin plant.
ConAgra Inc unit Swift and Co's pork plant in Worthington, Minn., will also be closed on Monday, company officials said.
